# Fetcher

> Typed HTTP clients, streaming, React hooks, and data viewers.

## Overview

- [TypeScript HTTP clients on native Fetch](/) — Use Fetcher for HTTP, service clients, streaming, and React data interactions.

## start

- [Choose your starting point](/start/) — Start with HTTP, a React request, or a local data table according to your existing application.
- [Install Fetcher](/start/installation) — Create an independent ESM project and install the core HTTP client.
- [Your first request](/start/first-request) — Run a typed JSON request and verify the HTTP 404 failure path.
- [Your first data view](/start/first-view) — Run a local Viewer and understand where data and saved state belong.
- [Choose your next task](/start/next-steps) — Extend the first successful request or table with one concrete application capability.

## guides

- [Build your application](/guides/) — Choose HTTP, service, stream, React, data-view, or integration tasks.

## guides/http

- [HTTP requests](/guides/http/) — Choose a concrete task for http requests.
- [Reuse a shared HTTP client](/guides/http/shared-client) — Configure a reusable origin, headers, and request timeout with explicit identity ownership.
- [Construct URLs, headers, and bodies](/guides/http/requests) — Send explicit path/query parameters and choose a body format appropriate to your server.
- [Choose and validate a result](/guides/http/results) — Select Response, exchange, or parsed JSON and verify what the caller actually receives.
- [Handle HTTP, transport, and parsing failures](/guides/http/failures) — Preserve exchange context and handle extraction failures at the application boundary.
- [Cancel requests and set timeouts](/guides/http/cancellation) — Assign AbortController ownership and distinguish response acquisition from full body deadlines.
- [Extend the request pipeline](/guides/http/interceptors) — Add and remove an owned interceptor at the stage where its input is available.

## guides/services

- [Service clients](/guides/services/) — Choose a concrete task for service clients.
- [Create a Declarative Service](/guides/services/declarative-client) — Define, call, and verify a decorator service with explicit request bindings.
- [Generate and Use an OpenAPI Client](/guides/services/generated-client) — Generate a real ItemsApiClient from a complete minimal schema and type-check its consumer.

## guides/streaming

- [Streaming data](/guides/streaming/) — Choose a concrete task for streaming data.
- [Read and close an event stream](/guides/streaming/sse) — Read and close an event stream — Fetcher
- [Stream a Chat Completion](/guides/streaming/chat) — Consume Chat Completions SSE through an application gateway with cancellation and reader cleanup.

## guides/react

- [React data flow](/guides/react/) — Choose a concrete task for react data flow.
- [Trigger and display a React request](/guides/react/requests) — Use the verified useFetcher component to render loading, results, errors, and cancellation.
- [Drive a query from input](/guides/react/queries) — Send a query as POST JSON and render the current component-owned result.
- [Debounce input-driven requests](/guides/react/debounce) — Delay changing input and distinguish queued execution from an active request.
- [Clean up React async work](/guides/react/cleanup) — Connect cancellation to the actual operation and distinguish abort, reset, and debounce cancellation.

## guides/view-engine

- [View Engine tasks](/guides/view-engine/) — Build a record page, configure filters and cells, and connect application-owned services.
- [Start a record page](/guides/view-engine/getting-started) — Run the local example and connect ViewDefinition, ViewInstance, ViewHost and ViewPage.
- [Configure filters](/guides/view-engine/filters) — Choose built-in editors, preserve component configuration, and apply queries explicitly.
- [Table and runtime operations](/guides/view-engine/table-and-runtime) — Configure built-in cells, column layout, summaries, refresh and page expansion.
- [Save and manage views](/guides/view-engine/saved-views) — Separate component configuration, service writes, user preferences and runtime state.
- [Add application extensions](/guides/view-engine/extensions) — Register global, table, row, filter and cell extensions with explicit ownership.

## guides/viewer

- [Data view tasks](/guides/viewer/) — Choose a concrete task for data view tasks.
- [Render local rows in a Viewer](/guides/viewer/local-data) — Build a backend-free table with a complete definition, initial view, and application-owned data.
- [Make pagination and sorting change rows](/guides/viewer/pagination-and-sorting) — Apply the requested condition and sort before slicing a one-based page.
- [Filter the displayed data](/guides/viewer/filters) — Connect an available filter, saved filter configuration, and an application query evaluator.
- [Save and restore view state](/guides/viewer/saved-views) — Implement view mutation callbacks and report success only after the chosen persistence accepts a change.
- [Connect remote rows to a Viewer](/guides/viewer/remote-data) — Render a paged Viewer with application-owned fetching, cancellation, and recoverable errors.

## guides/integrations

- [Platform integrations](/guides/integrations/) — Choose a concrete task for platform integrations.
- [Send a Wow Command and Read State](/guides/integrations/wow) — Configure application aggregate routes, inspect command results, and query or stream snapshot state.
- [Add CoSec Authentication](/guides/integrations/cosec) — Create a browser authentication session with refresh, token ownership, and cleanup.
- [Share State and Events](/guides/integrations/storage-and-events) — Verify local state and ordered events, then opt into browser tab notifications.

## architecture

- [Architecture and choices](/architecture/) — Choose the smallest client layer and identify the responsibilities that remain in your application.
- [Package boundaries](/architecture/package-boundaries) — Separate declared installation dependencies from runtime request paths and code generation.
- [Runtime support and SSR](/architecture/runtime-support) — Check platform capabilities and scope mutable identity state before sharing clients.
- [Request lifecycle](/architecture/request-lifecycle) — Place interception and extraction at the correct stage of a Fetcher request.
- [State and resource ownership](/architecture/state-and-resources) — Assign request state, table data, saved-view confirmation, and cleanup to their actual owners.
- [Failure model](/architecture/failure-model) — Handle transport, HTTP, extraction, Hook, and stream failures at the boundary where they occur.
- [Integration decisions](/architecture/integration-decisions) — Compare client styles and table layers by the contracts and maintenance they require.

## examples

- [Run complete examples](/examples/) — Run deterministic HTTP, React, Viewer, and View Engine examples with clear consumer and repository instructions.
- [Runnable HTTP example](/examples/http) — Run a local deterministic server and verify Fetcher success and HTTP failure behavior.
- [Runnable React request example](/examples/react) — Exercise successful, failed, and cancelled Fetcher requests with real React hook state.
- [Local Viewer example](/examples/viewer) — Filter, sort, page and save a local data view with application-owned state.
- [Complete View Engine example](/examples/view-engine) — A shared runnable record page with real local filtering, sorting and pagination.
